title: French Bulldog Hemivertebrae and Screw Tail: Spine Problems
description: French Bulldog hemivertebrae and screw tails: what veterinary studies show, why many findings have no symptoms, spinal warning signs and diagnostic tests.

faq.q: Do all French Bulldogs have hemivertebrae?
faq.a: No population-wide estimate establishes that. One hospital CT study detected them in 93.5% of a selected group of 62 neurologically normal French Bulldogs.

faq.q: Does a screw tail mean my Frenchie has spinal disease?
faq.a: A screw tail can share genetic associations with vertebral malformations, but the tail alone cannot diagnose spinal cord compression.
Some malformations are incidental. Severe spinal curvature or compression can produce progressive weakness or an abnormal gait; a veterinarian must evaluate the cause.
X-rays often identify bone malformations. CT and MRI may be needed to evaluate anatomy and spinal cord involvement if clinical signs are present.

faq.q: When should I seek urgent care?
faq.a: Sudden paralysis, inability to stand, or loss of bladder control needs immediate emergency veterinary assessment, regardless of the suspected cause.
